purpose: machine-facing subdomain knowledge base of concrete operations-research style work-units for optimization and planning under constraints (LP/IP, sensitivity & duality, project scheduling, forecasting & allocation), used by a knowledge-searcher meta-KB to locate, retrieve, evaluate, and synthesize how to model and decide under constraints
assumptions: no observed dataset or benchmark supplied; all metrics are heuristic priors
subdomain of Applied Math (Finance, Business, Design & Planning); scope is operations-research style optimization and planning math for business/design/planning
nodes are concrete modeling/optimization work-units (methods, decision areas, validation/control steps), not abstract topics
linear-programming-centric: nonlinear, stochastic, and metaheuristic optimization are largely out of scope
single-session-bounded work units suitable for heavy LLM-assisted execution and handoff
exclusions: nonlinear and convex programming beyond LP basics
full stochastic/robust optimization theory beyond scenario basics
advanced econometric forecasting (ARIMA/state-space) beyond moving averages/smoothing
supply-chain software implementation and solver internals at code level

glossary.definition: the set of all decision-variable values satisfying every constraint
the marginal change in the optimal objective per unit change in a constraint's right-hand side
a constraint satisfied with equality at the optimum (zero slack)
the longest-duration chain of activities with zero total float that sets project duration
the time an activity can slip without delaying the project (LS minus ES)
the time an activity can slip without delaying any successor's earliest start
the linear program obtained by dropping integrality on integer variables
study of how the optimal solution/objective changes with coefficient or RHS changes
the volume or revenue at which total revenue equals total cost
adjusting a schedule so resource usage stays within capacity over time
unit price minus unit variable cost, available to cover fixed costs
a plan chosen to perform acceptably across scenarios rather than optimally in one

evidence_label_policy.rule: all estimates are heuristic priors; observed_impact, data_quality, observed_co_occurrence = 0.0; posterior_importance = normalize(PI*EC)

source_registry.description: model heuristic priors for operations-research style optimization and planning math; no observed dataset supplied
source_registry.citation_or_locator: Hillier&Lieberman Introduction to Operations Research; Winston Operations Research: Applications and Algorithms; Vanderbei Linear Programming
grounding_limits: estimates are heuristic priors, not measured
no empirical calibration to a specific organization

nodes.definition: Translate an ambiguous business/planning situation into a well-posed optimization problem by naming decisions, objective sense, constraints, and time horizon.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: stakeholders reject the modeled objective as not matching the real goal

pros.claim: correct framing prevents optimizing the wrong objective
pros.example: choosing max throughput vs min cost changes the whole model

pros.claim: explicit decision/parameter split blocks later variable confusion
pros.example: marking labor hours as parameter not decision

cons.claim: over-scoping yields an intractable or unmaintainable model
cons.example: modeling 5-year horizon when 1 quarter is decision-relevant

cons.claim: premature numeric detail freezes a wrong structure
cons.example: hard-coding a demand figure before the goal is agreed

failure_modes: objective sense inverted (min coded as max)
decision variable confused with fixed parameter
acceptance_tests: objective sense matches stakeholder-confirmed goal
every decision variable is actionable (a real lever)
constraints trace to a real business limit

nodes.definition: Define the decision variables (continuous, integer, or binary) with units, bounds, and indexing that encode the actual levers of the plan.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a needed lever cannot be expressed with current variable set

pros.claim: clean indexing keeps the model scalable and readable
pros.example: x[p,t]=units of product p made in period t

pros.claim: correct variable type avoids fractional-unit nonsense
pros.example: binary y for open/close a facility

cons.claim: too many integer/binary variables explodes solve time
cons.example: binary per minute over a year

cons.claim: hidden unit mismatch corrupts every constraint
cons.example: mixing kg and tonnes in one variable family

failure_modes: continuous variable used where indivisibility required
index set omits a needed dimension
acceptance_tests: each variable maps to a real, controllable lever
types (int/binary/continuous) justified by divisibility
units consistent across all uses

nodes.definition: Construct the linear objective function that aggregates decision variables and cost/value coefficients into the single quantity to be optimized.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: optimal solution maximizes a proxy that diverges from true value

pros.claim: a single clear objective makes optimality well-defined
pros.example: minimize total production + holding cost

pros.claim: coefficient provenance enables later sensitivity analysis
pros.example: unit profit traced to margin report

cons.claim: scalarizing competing goals hides tradeoffs
cons.example: folding service level into cost with arbitrary weight

cons.claim: mis-scaled coefficients cause numerical instability
cons.example: mixing dollars and cents across terms

failure_modes: objective omits a material cost/value term
nonlinear value forced into a linear term
acceptance_tests: objective is linear in declared variables
coefficients trace to a sourced estimate
objective sense consistent with framing

nodes.definition: Encode resource limits, demand, balance, and policy rules as linear (in)equalities that define the feasible region.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a real-world rule is found unrepresented in the constraint set

pros.claim: explicit constraints make the feasible region auditable
pros.example: labor hours <= 4000 per week

pros.claim: big-M logical constraints encode on/off decisions
pros.example: production only if facility open: x<=M*y

cons.claim: a missing constraint yields an infeasible real plan
cons.example: ignoring a storage cap that the warehouse enforces

cons.claim: loose big-M values weaken the LP relaxation
cons.example: M set far larger than any feasible value

acceptance_tests: each constraint maps to a real limit or rule
feasible region is non-empty and bounded where expected
big-M values tight enough to be effective

nodes.definition: Characterize the feasible region: feasibility, boundedness, vertices, and degeneracy, before and after solving.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: solver reports infeasible or unbounded unexpectedly

pros.claim: detecting infeasibility early avoids chasing a phantom optimum
pros.example: spotting contradictory demand vs capacity

pros.claim: alternate-optima awareness prevents over-reading one solution
pros.example: two production plans with equal cost

cons.claim: degeneracy can stall or mislead pivot-based methods
cons.example: many tied basic feasible solutions

cons.claim: boundedness mistakes hide an unbounded objective
cons.example: forgetting an upper bound on a profitable variable

acceptance_tests: feasibility/boundedness explicitly verified
degeneracy and alternate optima flagged
vertices align with constraint geometry

nodes.definition: Solve the LP via simplex (or interior-point) and obtain primal optimal values, basis, and solver status with reproducible settings.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: solver returns a different basis/status after a model edit

pros.claim: simplex returns an exact vertex optimum and a usable basis
pros.example: optimal corner of a production polytope

pros.claim: reproducible solver settings make results auditable
pros.example: fixed seed and tolerance recorded

cons.claim: numerical tolerance issues can mislabel optimality
cons.example: near-degenerate pivots flagged as optimal too early

cons.claim: black-box trust hides modeling errors
cons.example: accepting an optimum to an infeasible-in-reality model

failure_modes: solver tolerance masks an ill-conditioned model
optimal basis not captured for sensitivity
acceptance_tests: solver status is optimal and recorded
primal solution satisfies all constraints
settings/tolerances logged for reproducibility

nodes.definition: Handle indivisibility and yes/no decisions with integer/binary variables, LP relaxation, and branch-and-bound basics.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: rounded LP solution proves infeasible or far from integer optimum

pros.claim: integer models capture real all-or-nothing decisions
pros.example: open exactly one of three depots

pros.claim: LP relaxation gives a valid bound to gauge optimality
pros.example: relaxation cost bounds the integer optimum

cons.claim: integer programs can be exponentially hard to solve
cons.example: large facility-location instance times out

cons.claim: naive rounding of LP solution is often infeasible/suboptimal
cons.example: rounding fractional truck counts breaks capacity

failure_modes: rounding LP relaxation instead of solving integer model
binary logic encoded with wrong big-M
acceptance_tests: integrality justified by real indivisibility
optimality gap reported and within tolerance
no naive rounding used as final answer

nodes.definition: Quantify how the optimal solution and objective respond to changes in coefficients and right-hand-sides (ranging, what-if).

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a coefficient moves outside its validated allowable range

pros.claim: sensitivity ranges show how robust the plan is
pros.example: profit stays optimal while margin varies +/-8%

pros.claim: what-if tables let planners pre-decide responses
pros.example: plan if demand rises 10%

cons.claim: ranges from one basis can be misread across degeneracy
cons.example: allowable range invalid once basis changes

cons.claim: simultaneous changes break single-coefficient ranges
cons.example: two coefficients changed beyond the 100% rule

failure_modes: allowable range applied beyond basis validity
acceptance_tests: ranges computed from the recorded optimal basis
simultaneous-change rule respected
what-if scenarios stay within validated ranges

nodes.definition: Derive and interpret the dual problem and shadow prices to value binding constraints and read marginal economics of the plan.

included: shadow price = dual value of a constraint

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a constraint's binding status flips after re-solve

pros.claim: shadow prices reveal where extra capacity is worth buying
pros.example: each extra labor hour adds $40 profit

pros.claim: reduced costs show why a product is not produced
pros.example: margin too low by $5 to enter the plan

cons.claim: shadow prices only hold within the RHS allowable range
cons.example: value collapses once 200 more hours added

cons.claim: integer-program shadow prices lack clean LP interpretation
cons.example: dual values unreliable after branching

failure_modes: shadow price extrapolated beyond allowable RHS range
acceptance_tests: shadow prices tied to currently binding constraints
values valid only within reported RHS ranges
reduced costs explain excluded variables
revisit_triggers: integer constraints added invalidating LP duals

nodes.definition: Identify binding constraints and bottlenecks that limit the objective, prioritizing them for managerial action.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: bottleneck shifts to a different resource after a change

pros.claim: targeting the binding constraint gives the biggest marginal gain
pros.example: add capacity only to the limiting machine

pros.claim: slack analysis avoids wasting money on non-binding resources
pros.example: ignore a resource with large unused slack

cons.claim: bottlenecks move once the current one is relieved
cons.example: relieving machine A makes B the new limit

cons.claim: single-bottleneck focus misses multi-constraint ties
cons.example: two constraints jointly binding

acceptance_tests: binding constraints derived from shadow prices/slack
action targets the highest-value binding limit
moving-bottleneck risk noted

nodes.definition: Model a project as activities with durations and precedence (AOA/AON network) suitable for critical-path computation.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a precedence relation is found wrong or missing

pros.claim: an explicit network makes scheduling math possible
pros.example: activities linked by finish-to-start edges

pros.claim: precedence discipline exposes hidden dependencies
pros.example: testing cannot start before build finishes

cons.claim: wrong precedence corrupts the whole schedule
cons.example: modeling parallel tasks as sequential

cons.claim: over-decomposition makes the network unwieldy
cons.example: hundreds of micro-activities

failure_modes: missing dependency hides a real constraint
acceptance_tests: network is acyclic with consistent duration units
precedence relations validated with the team
activity granularity is plannable

nodes.definition: Compute earliest/latest start-finish, the critical path, and total project duration via forward/backward pass.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: the critical path changes after a duration update

pros.claim: the critical path shows which delays move the deadline
pros.example: slip on critical task delays whole project

pros.claim: ES/EF/LS/LF table makes scheduling decisions explicit
pros.example: computing the latest safe start of a task

cons.claim: CPM ignores resource limits in its basic form
cons.example: two critical tasks need the same single crew

cons.claim: deterministic durations understate schedule risk
cons.example: fixed durations hide variance

failure_modes: critical path computed on a cyclic/invalid network
resource conflicts ignored on the path
acceptance_tests: forward/backward passes are arithmetically consistent
critical path has zero total float
project duration matches the longest path
revisit_triggers: resource conflicts surface on the path

nodes.definition: Compute total and free float (slack) for activities to find scheduling flexibility and protect the critical path.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a near-critical task consumes its float and becomes critical

pros.claim: float shows where delay is absorbable without slipping the deadline
pros.example: a task with 5 days float can wait

pros.claim: free float lets tasks move without affecting successors
pros.example: reschedule within free float safely

cons.claim: misusing total float can starve downstream tasks
cons.example: spending shared float twice

cons.claim: near-critical paths get ignored when only the critical path is watched
cons.example: a path with 1 day float slips

failure_modes: total float double-counted across a chain
acceptance_tests: total and free float computed consistently from CPM
near-critical activities flagged
shared float not allocated twice

nodes.definition: Turn the network/CPM result into a time-phased Gantt schedule and a baseline for tracking progress.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: actual progress diverges materially from the baseline

pros.claim: a Gantt communicates the schedule to non-technical stakeholders
pros.example: color-coded bars per workstream

pros.claim: a captured baseline enables variance tracking
pros.example: compare actual vs planned start dates

cons.claim: Gantt bars hide the underlying dependency logic
cons.example: moving a bar without honoring precedence

cons.claim: baselines drift if not formally re-baselined
cons.example: tracking against a stale baseline

acceptance_tests: Gantt dates reconcile with CPM ES/EF
working-calendar applied consistently
baseline captured before tracking begins

nodes.definition: Adjust the schedule to respect finite resource capacity (resource-constrained scheduling) while limiting deadline slippage.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a resource over-allocation reappears after a schedule change

pros.claim: leveling makes the plan executable with real crews
pros.example: spreading two parallel tasks to one shared team

pros.claim: leveling within float avoids extending the deadline
pros.example: shifting non-critical tasks only

cons.claim: resource-constrained scheduling is NP-hard; heuristics may be suboptimal
cons.example: greedy leveling extends project unnecessarily

cons.claim: leveling can silently extend the critical path
cons.example: consuming all float pushes the deadline

failure_modes: leveling pushes deadline without flagging it
priority rule biases resource assignment unfairly
acceptance_tests: no resource exceeds its capacity in any period
deadline impact of leveling is quantified
leveling first uses float before extending

nodes.definition: Produce demand/resource forecasts using basic time-series methods (moving averages, exponential smoothing, trend) with error tracking.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: forecast error exceeds its control limit for several periods

pros.claim: forecasts feed demand into the optimization/planning model
pros.example: predicted weekly demand sets the RHS

pros.claim: tracking forecast error exposes model drift
pros.example: rising MAPE signals a regime change

cons.claim: simple methods miss structural breaks and shocks
cons.example: moving average lags a sudden demand jump

cons.claim: forecast uncertainty propagates into every downstream decision
cons.example: over-trusting a point forecast in the LP

failure_modes: forecast point value used without its error band
seasonality ignored in a seasonal series
acceptance_tests: forecast method justified by series behavior
forecast error tracked against a control limit
uncertainty band carried into downstream use
revisit_triggers: new history invalidates the chosen method

nodes.definition: Compute break-even points and cost-volume-profit relationships to set feasible targets and guide go/no-go planning.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: cost structure or price changes the break-even point materially

pros.claim: break-even gives a clear minimum-viable target
pros.example: need 1,200 units/month to cover fixed cost

pros.claim: contribution margin guides product/price decisions
pros.example: drop products below positive margin

cons.claim: linear CVP ignores volume-dependent cost changes
cons.example: bulk discounts break the linear cost line

cons.claim: single-product break-even misleads in a product mix
cons.example: blended margin hides loss-makers

failure_modes: multi-product mix ignored in single-product formula
acceptance_tests: fixed vs variable costs correctly separated
break-even reconciles with the margin figures
margin of safety reported alongside break-even

nodes.definition: Optimally allocate scarce resources (budget, labor, capacity) across competing uses, often as an LP/knapsack-style allocation.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: resource budget or candidate returns change the optimal allocation

pros.claim: allocation by marginal return beats equal-split heuristics
pros.example: fund projects until budget exhausted by ROI

pros.claim: casting allocation as an LP makes tradeoffs explicit
pros.example: budget constraint plus per-use limits

cons.claim: allocation built on weak forecasts inherits their error
cons.example: ROI estimates off by 30%

cons.claim: indivisible allocations need integer methods, not LP
cons.example: cannot fund 0.4 of a project

acceptance_tests: allocation respects budget and per-use limits
indivisibility handled with integer methods when needed
sensitivity of allocation to returns reported

nodes.definition: Stress plans against alternative scenarios and parameter uncertainty to choose robust rather than merely optimal solutions.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: the optimal plan performs poorly under a plausible scenario

pros.claim: robust plans survive forecast error better than knife-edge optima
pros.example: plan good across +/-20% demand

pros.claim: scenario rollups expose fragile assumptions
pros.example: optimum collapses if a supplier fails

cons.claim: robustness usually costs some expected-case optimality
cons.example: paying for slack capacity

cons.claim: too many scenarios become unmanageable and diluted
cons.example: dozens of equally-weighted scenarios

failure_modes: robustness traded away silently for optimality
acceptance_tests: plan evaluated across best/base/worst scenarios
chosen plan justified on a robustness criterion
fragility to key parameters documented

nodes.definition: Validate the optimization/planning model end-to-end: feasibility, unit consistency, sanity bounds, and back-testing against known cases.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a back-test reveals the model contradicts a known correct outcome

pros.claim: validation catches modeling errors before they drive bad plans
pros.example: back-test reproduces last quarter's known optimum

pros.claim: unit checks catch silent coefficient mistakes
pros.example: detecting a cost entered per-unit vs per-batch

cons.claim: validation adds cycle time before a plan can ship
cons.example: extra week of back-testing

cons.claim: over-fitting validation to known cases hides novel errors
cons.example: passing only the cases you thought of

acceptance_tests: units consistent across objective and constraints
model reproduces at least one known-correct case
implausible solutions are investigated, not accepted
revisit_triggers: new data invalidates a prior back-test

nodes.definition: Translate the validated optimization output into an auditable recommendation with assumptions, sensitivities, and a decision record for stakeholders.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: stakeholders act on a recommendation whose assumptions later prove false

pros.claim: a decision record makes the plan auditable and accountable
pros.example: logged assumptions and approver

pros.claim: surfacing sensitivities prevents over-trust in a single number
pros.example: showing the plan's robust range

cons.claim: a confident recommendation can mask deep model uncertainty
cons.example: one headline number hides wide bands

cons.claim: irreversible commitments are hard to undo if the model was wrong
cons.example: capital spent on a wrong bottleneck

failure_modes: sensitivities hidden behind a single number
irreversible decision made without human review
acceptance_tests: recommendation lists assumptions and validated ranges
sensitivity/robustness summary attached
decision record signed before irreversible commitment

edges.why_related: variables can only be defined after decisions and scope are framed
edges.risk_of_conflict: premature variables encode a wrong frame
edges.example: levers chosen after objective sense fixed
edges.resolution_rule: source dominates: re-frame before redefining variables

edges.why_related: objective is expressed over the declared variables
edges.benefit_of_coupling: consistent variable basis for the objective
edges.risk_of_conflict: objective terms reference undefined variables
edges.resolution_rule: variables dominate: fix variable set before coefficients

edges.why_related: constraints are written over the declared variables
edges.benefit_of_coupling: shared variable dictionary keeps constraints consistent
edges.risk_of_conflict: constraints reference variables that do not exist
edges.resolution_rule: variables dominate: stabilize variables before constraints

edges.why_related: feasible region analysis needs the objective to assess optimization direction
edges.risk_of_conflict: analyzing region without objective misses unboundedness
edges.example: unbounded only matters given a profitable direction
edges.resolution_rule: sequence: define objective before judging boundedness

edges.why_related: the feasible region is defined by the constraint set
edges.risk_of_conflict: region analysis on incomplete constraints is invalid
edges.resolution_rule: constraints dominate: complete constraints before region claims

edges.why_related: solving requires a verified non-empty bounded region
edges.benefit_of_coupling: feasibility check prevents solving a phantom model
edges.risk_of_conflict: solving an infeasible model wastes effort
edges.example: simplex needs a feasible starting region
edges.resolution_rule: region dominates: verify feasibility before solving

edges.why_related: the solver optimizes the declared objective
edges.risk_of_conflict: wrong objective yields a confidently wrong optimum
edges.resolution_rule: objective dominates: confirm objective before trusting optimum

edges.why_related: the solver enforces the declared constraints
edges.risk_of_conflict: missing constraints give an infeasible-in-reality optimum
edges.resolution_rule: constraints dominate: finalize constraints before solving

edges.why_related: integer methods build on the LP relaxation solved by simplex
edges.risk_of_conflict: branching without a relaxation bound is blind
edges.resolution_rule: relaxation dominates: solve LP relaxation before branching

edges.why_related: sensitivity ranges are computed from the optimal basis
edges.risk_of_conflict: ranges computed without the basis are invalid
edges.resolution_rule: basis dominates: capture basis before ranging

edges.why_related: dual values/shadow prices come from the solved primal
edges.risk_of_conflict: shadow prices without a valid primal are meaningless
edges.example: dual values read from the optimal basis
edges.resolution_rule: primal dominates: solve primal before reading duals

edges.why_related: binding constraints are identified via positive shadow prices/zero slack
edges.risk_of_conflict: calling a non-binding constraint a bottleneck wastes capex
edges.example: positive shadow price flags a binding limit
edges.resolution_rule: duality dominates: use dual values to classify binding constraints

edges.why_related: the project network is scoped by the framed planning problem
edges.risk_of_conflict: an unscoped network sprawls or omits work
edges.example: activities derived from the planning scope
edges.resolution_rule: framing dominates: scope before activity decomposition

edges.why_related: critical path is computed on the activity network
edges.benefit_of_coupling: the network is the input to CPM
edges.risk_of_conflict: CPM on a cyclic/invalid network is wrong
edges.resolution_rule: network dominates: validate network before CPM

edges.why_related: float is derived from CPM start/finish times
edges.risk_of_conflict: float computed without CPM is unsupported
edges.resolution_rule: CPM dominates: compute CPM before float

edges.why_related: the Gantt baseline is time-phased from CPM results
edges.benefit_of_coupling: CPM dates anchor the Gantt bars
edges.risk_of_conflict: a Gantt detached from CPM violates precedence
edges.resolution_rule: CPM dominates: reconcile Gantt to CPM dates

edges.why_related: float informs where Gantt bars can flex
edges.benefit_of_coupling: float guides bar placement and buffers
edges.risk_of_conflict: ignoring float over-constrains the Gantt
edges.resolution_rule: sequence: compute float before finalizing Gantt

edges.why_related: leveling adjusts the baselined schedule for resource limits
edges.benefit_of_coupling: baseline is the starting point for leveling
edges.risk_of_conflict: leveling without a baseline cannot measure slippage
edges.resolution_rule: baseline dominates: capture baseline before leveling

edges.why_related: available float bounds how far leveling can shift tasks without slipping
edges.benefit_of_coupling: float is the budget for leveling moves
edges.risk_of_conflict: leveling beyond float silently extends the deadline
edges.resolution_rule: float bounds leveling: extend deadline only with explicit approval

edges.why_related: forecasting scope follows the framed planning horizon
edges.risk_of_conflict: forecasting an irrelevant horizon wastes effort
edges.resolution_rule: framing dominates: set horizon before forecasting

edges.why_related: forecasts feed demand/return estimates into allocation
edges.risk_of_conflict: allocation inherits forecast error
edges.resolution_rule: forecast feeds allocation: propagate forecast error into allocation

edges.why_related: break-even targets are set within the framed cost/goal structure
edges.benefit_of_coupling: framing supplies cost and goal context
edges.risk_of_conflict: break-even on the wrong cost frame misleads targets
edges.example: break-even tied to the planning goal
edges.resolution_rule: framing dominates: confirm cost structure before break-even

edges.why_related: allocation is an objective-driven optimization sharing LP structure
edges.risk_of_conflict: treating them as unrelated duplicates modeling effort
edges.example: both maximize return subject to limits
edges.resolution_rule: similarity: reuse LP objective patterns in allocation

edges.why_related: allocation respects budget/capacity constraints
edges.risk_of_conflict: allocation ignoring constraints overspends
edges.resolution_rule: constraints dominate: bound allocation by real limits

edges.why_related: robustness analysis extends single-change sensitivity to full scenarios
edges.risk_of_conflict: scenarios inconsistent with sensitivity ranges mislead
edges.resolution_rule: sensitivity dominates: ground scenarios in validated ranges

edges.why_related: forecast uncertainty drives the scenario spread
edges.risk_of_conflict: ignoring forecast uncertainty yields fragile plans
edges.resolution_rule: forecast feeds scenarios: size scenarios by forecast error

edges.why_related: robustness testing can trigger revisiting the allocation
edges.risk_of_conflict: unbounded re-allocation loops waste cycles
edges.resolution_rule: feedback stop: re-allocate at most twice unless materiality threshold exceeded

edges.why_related: validation checks the solved model before it is trusted
edges.benefit_of_coupling: solving precedes validation of the solution
edges.risk_of_conflict: shipping an unvalidated optimum risks bad plans
edges.resolution_rule: sequence: solve then validate before handoff

edges.why_related: integer solutions must be validated for feasibility/plausibility
edges.risk_of_conflict: an unvalidated integer plan may be infeasible in practice
edges.resolution_rule: sequence: validate integer solutions before acceptance

edges.why_related: dual/shadow-price plausibility is part of validation
edges.benefit_of_coupling: economic sanity checks validate the model
edges.risk_of_conflict: implausible shadow prices signal modeling errors
edges.example: negative shadow price on a costly resource flagged
edges.resolution_rule: sequence: sanity-check duals during validation

edges.why_related: a recommendation may only be handed off after validation passes
edges.risk_of_conflict: handing off an unvalidated plan risks irreversible loss
edges.resolution_rule: validation dominates: no handoff before validation passes

edges.why_related: the handoff must report robustness/sensitivity to decision-makers
edges.risk_of_conflict: a recommendation without robustness invites over-trust
edges.example: attach scenario comparison to the recommendation
edges.resolution_rule: robustness dominates: include robustness before sign-off

edges.why_related: bottleneck findings shape the managerial recommendation
edges.risk_of_conflict: omitting bottlenecks weakens the recommendation
edges.example: recommend capex on the binding machine
edges.resolution_rule: sequence: surface bottlenecks in the handoff

edges.why_related: pushing the objective harder strains feasibility against constraints
edges.risk_of_conflict: an aggressive objective can make the model infeasible
edges.example: max profit collides with capacity limit
edges.resolution_rule: constraints dominate feasibility: relax objective targets, never violate hard limits

edges.why_related: integrality requirements trade solve speed against exactness
edges.benefit_of_coupling: exact integers vs fast LP solve
edges.risk_of_conflict: demanding exact integers can blow the time budget
edges.example: branch-and-bound times out vs quick LP
edges.resolution_rule: risk dominates: accept a bounded optimality gap before missing the planning deadline

edges.why_related: resource leveling can extend the critical path and deadline
edges.risk_of_conflict: leveling silently lengthens the project
edges.example: leveling pushes the finish date out
edges.resolution_rule: deadline policy dominates: extend duration only with explicit stakeholder approval

edges.why_related: robust plans sacrifice some optimal expected-case allocation
edges.risk_of_conflict: over-hedging wastes resources; under-hedging is fragile
edges.example: holding slack capacity vs full allocation
edges.resolution_rule: risk tolerance dominates: choose robustness level per stakeholder risk appetite

edges.why_related: forecast optimism vs conservative break-even targets create tension
edges.risk_of_conflict: optimistic forecasts set unreachable break-even targets
edges.example: forecast > break-even but at high risk
edges.resolution_rule: conservatism dominates for go/no-go: use conservative forecast band for break-even commitments

edges.why_related: validation rigor competes with speed-to-decision
edges.risk_of_conflict: rushing handoff skips validation; over-validating misses the window
edges.example: skipping back-test to hit a deadline
edges.resolution_rule: validation dominates: never hard-lock a recommendation before validation passes

conflict_axes.trigger: objective targets approach or breach hard constraint limits
resolution_order: escalate if hard limits block the goal
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: hard constraints win over objective ambition; never violate a real limit to hit a target
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: objective is unattainable without breaching a hard constraint
conflict_axes.example: max-profit plan is infeasible until a capacity assumption is relaxed

conflict_axes.trigger: branch-and-bound exceeds the time budget chasing the exact integer optimum
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: deadline-bounded planning accepts a documented optimality gap over a missed deadline
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: remaining gap is large enough to flip the decision
conflict_axes.example: facility-location solve times out at 5% gap

conflict_axes.trigger: resource leveling lengthens the critical path beyond the target deadline
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: executable resourcing wins, but any deadline extension requires explicit approval
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: leveling extends the deadline beyond the committed date
conflict_axes.example: two parallel critical tasks need one crew

conflict_axes.trigger: the expected-case optimum performs poorly under plausible scenarios
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: risk tolerance sets the robustness level; severe downside overrides expected-case gains
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: worst-case loss exceeds stakeholder risk appetite
conflict_axes.example: knife-edge optimum collapses if demand drops 15%

conflict_axes.trigger: an optimistic forecast sets break-even/commitment targets that are unlikely
resolution_order: escalate if targets depend on the optimistic tail
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: go/no-go commitments use the conservative forecast band, not the point estimate
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: decision flips between optimistic and conservative forecast bands
conflict_axes.example: target met only if demand hits the 90th percentile

conflict_axes.trigger: a decision deadline pressures shipping the plan before validation completes
resolution_order: escalate if validation is incomplete at deadline
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: validation gate dominates: no irreversible handoff before mandatory validation passes
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: validation incomplete at an irreversible commitment point
conflict_axes.example: quarter-end forces sign-off before back-test finishes

conflict_axes.trigger: adding realism (constraints, integrality) makes the model intractable
resolution_order: add fidelity only where it changes the decision
escalate if needed fidelity is intractable
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: decision-relevant fidelity wins; drop detail that does not change the recommendation
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: needed realism cannot be solved within budget
conflict_axes.example: per-minute binary variables make the model unsolvable

conflict_axes.trigger: shadow prices are extrapolated beyond their valid RHS range
resolution_order: bound shadow-price use to allowable range
escalate if a large change is required
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: range validity dominates: never apply a shadow price outside its allowable RHS interval
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: the proposed change exceeds the allowable RHS range
conflict_axes.example: valuing 500 extra hours when the range covers only 100

conflict_axes.trigger: an automated optimum drives an irreversible or high-stakes commitment
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: human review dominates automation for irreversible, high-risk, or low-confidence decisions
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: irreversibility or risk crosses the review threshold
conflict_axes.example: auto-recommended capital spend on a bottleneck

edge_cases.failure_mode: solver returns infeasible and work stalls
edge_cases.example: demand exceeds total capacity yet a demand-satisfaction equality is required
edge_cases.detection_method: solver status = infeasible; run an IIS/constraint-relaxation diagnostic
resolution: relax or correct the offending constraint

edge_cases.trigger: a profitable variable lacks an upper bound
edge_cases.failure_mode: solver reports unbounded; no usable optimum
edge_cases.example: maximize profit with no capacity cap on a profitable product
edge_cases.detection_method: solver status = unbounded; check for missing bounds/constraints
resolution: add the missing bound or constraint

edge_cases.trigger: an LP-relaxation solution is rounded to integers as the final answer
edge_cases.failure_mode: rounded plan is infeasible or far from optimum
edge_cases.example: rounding fractional truck counts violates a capacity constraint
edge_cases.detection_method: compare rounded objective and feasibility against a true integer solve

edge_cases.trigger: a shadow price is applied beyond its allowable RHS range
edge_cases.failure_mode: capacity decisions valued with an invalid marginal price
edge_cases.example: valuing 500 extra labor hours when the range only covers 100
edge_cases.detection_method: compare the proposed RHS change against the reported allowable range
resolution: limit shadow-price use to the valid range

edge_cases.trigger: the activity network contains a precedence cycle
edge_cases.failure_mode: CPM cannot compute a valid critical path
edge_cases.example: task A waits on B while B waits on A
edge_cases.detection_method: topological-sort the network; a failure indicates a cycle
resolution: break the cycle by correcting a precedence relation

edge_cases.trigger: shared total float is consumed by multiple tasks independently
edge_cases.failure_mode: the schedule slips despite apparent float
edge_cases.example: two tasks on one path each 'use' the same 3 days of float
edge_cases.detection_method: track float consumption per path, not per task
resolution: allocate shared float once per path

edge_cases.trigger: resource leveling extends the deadline without flagging it
edge_cases.failure_mode: stakeholders commit to an already-slipped date
edge_cases.example: greedy leveling pushes the finish date out by two weeks silently
edge_cases.detection_method: compare post-leveling finish date against the baseline finish date
resolution: quantify the deadline delta from leveling

edge_cases.trigger: a point forecast is used without its error band
edge_cases.failure_mode: downstream plan is fragile to forecast error
edge_cases.example: the LP RHS uses a single demand number that proves 25% high
edge_cases.detection_method: check that forecast uncertainty bands are carried into downstream use
resolution: re-plan if error breaches control limits

edge_cases.example: cost entered per-batch while variables are per-unit
edge_cases.detection_method: dimensional/unit consistency check across objective and constraints
resolution: normalize all coefficients to consistent units
add a unit check to validation

edge_cases.trigger: degeneracy/alternate optima make sensitivity ranges non-unique
edge_cases.example: multiple optimal bases give different allowable ranges
edge_cases.detection_method: detect zero-slack basic variables / multiple optimal bases
resolution: re-solve with anti-degeneracy or note caveat

edge_cases.trigger: an irreversible commitment is made on an unvalidated/low-confidence model
edge_cases.failure_mode: large loss if the model was wrong
edge_cases.example: capital is committed to the wrong bottleneck before validation
edge_cases.detection_method: check human_review_required and validation status before irreversible actions

dominance_rules.rule: risk control dominates speed for high-risk planning decisions
dominance_rules.example: shipping a capex plan before back-testing

dominance_rules.rule: true prerequisites are sequenced before higher-value-but-blocked work
dominance_rules.example: solving before constraints are finalized is forbidden

dominance_rules.rule: correct heuristic labeling dominates false numeric precision
dominance_rules.required_action: keep heuristic labels; do not fabricate observed data
dominance_rules.example: never label estimated coefficients as observed

dominance_rules.rule: QA/validation dominates the desire to lock an artifact
dominance_rules.required_action: no hard lock before validation passes

dominance_rules.rule: human review dominates automation for irreversible or high-risk decisions

dominance_rules.required_action: relax targets, never violate hard limits
dominance_rules.example: infeasible max-profit target must yield to capacity

dominance_rules.trigger: committed deadline vs silent leveling slip
dominance_rules.rule: committed deadlines dominate silent leveling extensions
dominance_rules.required_action: quantify and approve any leveling slippage
dominance_rules.example: leveling pushes the finish date without sign-off

dominance_rules.trigger: RHS range validity vs shadow-price use
dominance_rules.required_action: limit shadow prices to their valid range
dominance_rules.example: valuing changes beyond the allowable RHS range

dominance_rules.rule: schema/reference integrity dominates raw object volume
dominance_rules.required_action: never pad with invalid or duplicate objects
dominance_rules.example: adding near-duplicate nodes just to hit a count

dominance_rules.rule: every object must trace to a source, question, or node
dominance_rules.required_action: drop objects that cannot be traced
dominance_rules.example: an edge with no resolvable endpoints is removed

anti_rework_rules.rule: do not build variables/constraints before framing is agreed
anti_rework_rules.rationale: framing errors cascade into every downstream object
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: variables added before objective sense is confirmed
anti_rework_rules.example: coding constraints before the goal is agreed

anti_rework_rules.rule: do not write the objective/constraints before variables are stable
anti_rework_rules.rationale: objective/constraint terms must reference defined variables
anti_rework_rules.example: summing over an index set that is later changed

anti_rework_rules.rule: do not solve before feasibility/boundedness is checked
anti_rework_rules.rationale: solving an infeasible/unbounded model wastes effort
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: solver run on an unverified region
anti_rework_rules.example: chasing an optimum to an infeasible model

anti_rework_rules.rule: do not compute sensitivity/duals before the basis is captured
anti_rework_rules.rationale: post-optimal analysis is invalid without the optimal basis
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: ranges reported without a recorded basis
anti_rework_rules.example: shadow prices read from a stale solve

anti_rework_rules.rule: do not run CPM before the network is validated acyclic
anti_rework_rules.rationale: CPM on an invalid network produces a wrong critical path
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: CPM run on a network with a precedence cycle
anti_rework_rules.example: computing duration on a cyclic network

anti_rework_rules.rule: do not level resources before CPM/float are computed
anti_rework_rules.rationale: leveling without float cannot measure slippage
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: leveling applied before float is known
anti_rework_rules.example: shifting tasks with no float budget

anti_rework_rules.rule: do not allocate on forecasts lacking error bands
anti_rework_rules.rationale: allocation inherits and amplifies forecast error
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: allocation uses a point forecast with no band
anti_rework_rules.example: budget set on a single demand number

anti_rework_rules.rule: do not hand off a recommendation before validation passes
anti_rework_rules.rationale: an unvalidated recommendation risks irreversible loss
anti_rework_rules.example: signing off before unit checks complete

anti_rework_rules.rule: do not make irreversible commitments before human review
anti_rework_rules.rationale: irreversible errors cannot be cheaply undone

anti_rework_rules.rule: record a validation-report entry after every major repair
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: a model edit with no validation_report entry
